title: Sell Mineral Rights in Lochbuie, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lochbuie, CO | Weld-Adams Wattenberg Edge
metaDescription: Hold minerals near fast-growing Lochbuie, CO? We track Wattenberg-area wells now surrounded by new subdivisions and quote against real production data.
heroLead: Lochbuie has grown from a quiet Weld County crossroads into one of the fastest-expanding suburbs on the DJ Basin's southern edge, with new subdivisions now sitting near well pads drilled a decade or more before the houses arrived.
intro: If you own minerals near Lochbuie, you've watched the area change fast — rooftops spreading across what used to be open farmland, right up against Wattenberg field spacing units that were drilled and producing well before the growth boom. That collision between residential expansion and existing oil and gas infrastructure is now a defining fact of this part of Weld County.

sections.heading: Existing wells versus new development pressure
paragraphs: Wells that were permitted and drilled here years ago are generally grandfathered under prior rules even as surrounding setback and local control standards have tightened since SB 19-181 passed in 2019. That means an established Lochbuie-area well can keep producing on its existing schedule even though a brand-new well proposed today, near the same houses, would face a much tougher permitting path.
For mineral owners, that's mostly good news: your interest's value depends on the well that's already there and its decline trend, not on whether new drilling could happen nearby in the future.

sections.heading: How we price a Lochbuie interest
paragraphs: We pull the specific well's COGCC production record, check whether your acreage sits in one spacing unit or has been pooled across several as pad development consolidated leases over time, and quote against actual paid volumes and current decline stage rather than a flat number for the area.

faqs.question: Will new subdivisions affect the wells already producing near Lochbuie?
faqs.answer: Existing wells generally continue operating under the rules in place when they were permitted. Growth mostly affects the likelihood of new drilling nearby, not existing production.

faqs.question: How do I find out which well my interest is tied to?
faqs.answer: Send your legal description and we'll match it against COGCC well and unit records for the area.

faqs.question: My royalty checks have dropped over the past few years — is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's the expected decline pattern for Wattenberg horizontals. We factor the well's specific decline curve into any valuation rather than pricing off an old peak.

faqs.question: Does living next to new construction affect my mineral interest at all?
faqs.answer: Only indirectly, through the local setback rules that could apply to any future well proposal. It doesn't change what an existing well has already produced or what your interest is currently worth.
